brief: Goldman's Ryan Sharkey and Prime Services team (Vinny Lin, Chris Lucas, Ty Klein, Lee Coppersmith, Vani Ranganath) frame the AI-stock selloff as machine-driven, not discretionary panic. The Democratic sweep put AI/data-center regulation back on the table, and Thursday's crash (NDX -6.36%, worst since Covid) hit AI baskets hardest while the S&P ex-AI fell only 0.3%. Evidence for the machine thesis: ETF shorts jumped 7% while single-stock de-grossing stayed modest, CTAs are modeled to keep selling even in a flat tape, and levered ETFs saw record inflows the day before the crash. Hedge funds de-grossed, yet gross leverage rose because mark-to-market losses shrank fund equity faster than exposure fell; weekly net Tech selling hit $6bn, cumulatively far exceeding July's unwind, and TMT funds wiped out their 2026 gains. Against that, corporate buybacks run near $5bn/day with 90% of the S&P back in its open window, a flow Goldman says roughly matches CTA supply in a flat tape and beats it over a month. The piece's view: that balance holds only if Tuesday's CPI stays cool; a hot print pushes CTA selling into its down-tape scenario and adds a December hike, so every bounce should be treated as a sell-the-rip until buyers beyond CFOs and models show up.
